segments.source: Verve calls Streetlevel its original all-purpose blend and lists Honduras, Guatemala and Colombia on the current page. It rates the roast medium at 6/10. The page does not specify one complete variety or processing record for all components. Avoid treating the three country names as a permanent farm list; check the delivered bag.

segments.source: Clementine, red apple and honeycomb are Verve’s descriptors. They signal a sweeter, fruit-forward medium profile, not sensory findings from Coffeedant. An older independent café/bag tasting described its own Streetlevel sample; it cannot confirm today’s blend or quantify consistency.

segments.source: Owner accounts include a disappointing espresso and another very negative bag impression. They are self-selected, use different equipment and dates, and cannot support a defect rate. They do show why a first small bag and a deliberate espresso dial-in are more useful than assuming a well-known blend suits every palate.

segments.source: Verve markets Streetlevel across brewing methods, including espresso. Use a separate dose, water ratio and grind for filter versus a portafilter; a single “all-purpose” product description does not imply one universal setting. The current product page’s preferred brew messaging is an invitation to experiment, not a measured Coffeedant result.

segments.source: If you make both a morning drip pot and afternoon espresso, choose a grinder that can return to a marked setting, keep whole beans sealed and document each recipe. A fruit cue that reads pleasantly in filter may be more challenging in a short espresso shot; adjust on the actual bag rather than assuming a fixed outcome.

segments.source: Streetlevel’s case is flexible device positioning plus a clear medium fruit-and-honey brief. If your household only drinks traditional dark lattes, its broad-use framing does not by itself justify the bag over a darker, explicitly milk-oriented coffee.

segments.source: Stumptown Hair Bender is another multi-method espresso blend with a different roaster profile. Onyx Geometry goes lighter with published exact filter and espresso starts. Streetlevel is the medium, accessible all-purpose option here, but no controlled tasting ranks them.

segments.source: For milk drinks, consult the separate milk-bean guide, which distinguishes large lattes from small cappuccinos. Verve’s fruit language may suit one drink size and disappear in another; only a repeatable personal brew can answer that.

segments.source: Streetlevel is a useful one-bag candidate for someone moving among espresso, drip and immersion methods who likes a medium roast with fruit and honey in Verve’s flavor brief. Its current origin panel is clear at country level, but the blend lacks complete variety and process detail. An all-purpose label cannot replace separate brew recipes. Start with a smaller whole-bean pack and let the delivered bag and your repeatable recipe decide any larger order.
